topic.angle: Why a receiver needs four satellites: three coordinates plus its own clock error

card.title: GPS needs four satellites, not three

body.claim: A GPS receiver normally needs signals from at least four satellites to find where you are.
body.why: Each satellite broadcasts its position and the time. The receiver turns each signal delay into a range, using the speed of light. Three satellites give three coordinates, but the receiver also has to solve for the error in its own clock, so there are four unknowns.

probes.question: Why does a GPS receiver normally need four satellites?
options: It solves for three position coordinates and its own clock error
Each satellite covers one compass direction
Four is the most a phone can hear

probes.question: In the simplified picture, the spheres around three satellites typically intersect at how many points?

claims.claim: A GPS receiver normally needs at least four satellites (title, claim, probe 1 answer)
claims.quote: at a minimum, four satellites must be in view of the receiver for it to compute four unknown quantities

claims.claim: Four unknowns: three position coordinates plus the receiver's clock error (why)
claims.quote: three position coordinates and the deviation of its own clock from satellite time

claims.claim: Each satellite broadcasts its position and the time
claims.quote: of its own position and time, and broadcasts that data continuously

claims.claim: Receiver turns signal delay into range using the speed of light
claims.quote: the receiver forms four time of flight (TOF) values, which are (given the speed of light) approximately equivalent to receiver-satellite ranges

claims.claim: Probe 2: in the simplified picture three satellite spheres typically intersect at two points
claims.quote: Signals from at minimum three satellites are required, and their three spheres would typically intersect at two points.
